name: Robust Send Plan
description: Keep provider-wide request-level Live LLM calls close to the saved provider max-inflight limit when ready work exists, using shared provider admission leases, exact request-attempt lifecycle recovery, adaptive scheduling, and explicit telemetry without changing provider or model settings.

userStories.title: Add canonical provider key helper
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one canonical provider bucket helper so scheduler, request runtime, telemetry, and job-detail UI count provider capacity the same way.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement one canonical `providerKey` helper used by add-to-queue ready-target bucketing, scheduler, endpoint availability, connection health, dispatch runtime, request runtime, telemetry, and job-detail read models.
Provider key precedence is saved `providerConnectionId`, deterministic owner-backed synthetic provider id, `codex:default`, then provider-scoped non-Codex default key.
Non-Codex default buckets are shared per provider across models but never globally across unrelated providers.
Missing provider connection ids do not collapse to `unknown` when a synthetic or default provider bucket is available.

userStories.title: Add endpoint availability key helper
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want endpoint availability keyed separately from provider admission so one unhealthy endpoint does not block healthy sibling endpoints under the same provider bucket.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement canonical `endpointAvailabilityKey` using `providerKey` plus normalized endpoint identity for saved, synthetic, and default provider buckets.
Normalize endpoint identity by canonicalizing scheme, host, default port, meaningful path, and `/v1` suffix while rejecting credentials, query strings, and fragments as misconfigured.
Distinct meaningful paths such as `/openai/v1` and `/v1` remain distinct endpoint availability keys.

Endpoint-less Codex app-server capacity uses one `codex://app-server` identity and may skip HTTP probing; non-Codex HTTP/default buckets do not skip probing solely because `providerConnectionId` is null.

userStories.title: Return owner provider bucket snapshots
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want owner-backed running-job and runtime APIs to provide immutable provider bucket snapshots before claims so request admission uses a current provider limit version.
acceptanceCriteria: Running-job and runtime APIs return canonical `providerKey`, deterministic synthetic provider id when needed, provider name/family, configured `maxInflightRequests`, resolved default capacity, `providerLimit`, and `providerLimitVersion` before claims are made.
Prompt-local invocation context no longer invents synthetic provider ids or recomputes admission buckets after claim.
Saved provider setting changes issue a new bucket snapshot/version and stale acquire callers refresh instead of admitting under an old limit.
Provider-limit tests cover null `maxInflightRequests`, stale `providerLimitVersion`, stale same-holder snapshot advisories, limit decrease drain-down, and stable synthetic ids across owner restart.

userStories.title: Add request attempt manifest schema
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want durable request-attempt manifests on existing prompt and claim surfaces so request lifecycle recovery can identify exact attempts without a new lifecycle table.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `request_attempt_manifest_json` and `request_attempt_manifest_version` to local `queue_prompt` and judge-worker `accepted_claim` surfaces that lack them.

Add request-attempt-aware JSON columns to `app.token_use`, local `judgment_outbox`, local `completion_ack`, `pending_token_use`, `completion_outbox`, owner completion request bodies, and owner token-use import request bodies.

Each request-attempt JSON entry stores `requestAttemptId`, `providerKey`, prompt or claim id, outcome, closeout kind, optional base URL, token counts, timestamps, error fields, and durable closeout reference as applicable.
`pending_token_use` identity includes at least job id, queue record id, and request attempt id plus owner/claim routing fields needed for delivery.

userStories.title: Implement manifest CAS writes and compaction
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want atomic manifest merge and bounded retention so sibling attempts are preserved and terminal attempt metadata stays durable without unbounded growth.
acceptanceCriteria: Manifest writes use compare-and-swap: reload current JSON/version, merge by `requestAttemptId`, and increment version only when the expected version matches.
Required manifest writes occur before slot wait, when entering live request, when entering persistence, and on closeout; high-frequency age samples remain in memory.
CAS exhaustion writes a durable manifest repair marker on the owning prompt or claim before the prompt/claim becomes non-schedulable in persistence repair.
Concurrent chunked-attempt writes preserve sibling entries and reload/retry bounded conflicts before surfacing invariant failure.
Terminal manifest entries compact only after token-use, outbox, ack, import, or equivalent closeout evidence is durably recoverable.

userStories.title: Enforce request attempt state machine
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want request-attempt lifecycle states to be monotonic and exact so retry, requeue, worker-loss, and persistence recovery do not fabricate prompt success or failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Define request-attempt states `waitingForRequestSlot`, `liveRequest`, `persistingCompletion`, `completedRequest`, `closedRequest`, `telemetryUnavailable`, and `workerUnavailable` separately from prompt lifecycle states.
Valid transitions are monotonic, with `completedRequest` and `closedRequest` as terminal sinks except for idempotent same-state metadata enrichment.
Later exact durable evidence may supersede `telemetryUnavailable` or `workerUnavailable`; late evidence after `closedRequest(workerLostNoDurableResult)` is quarantined as a conflict.
Duplicate attempt ids with conflicting provider, ownership, outcome, token totals, closeout kind, durable closeout reference, or normalized timestamps are invariant failures.

userStories.title: Make completion persistence exact-attempt aware
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want token-use, outbox, completion journal, and owner ack/import persistence to close exact request attempts instead of relying on aggregate request counts.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace count-only closeout such as `markJudgmentRequestsPersisted(jobId, count)` with request-attempt-aware persisted and closed APIs that accept exact `requestAttemptId`s.

Token-use persistence, pending token-use, local judgment outbox payloads, completion outbox payloads, completion ack rows, owner completion/import request bodies, and imported token-use rows carry exact `requestAttemptId`s through `request_attempts_json`.
Chunked judging and retries persist and close multiple attempts for the same prompt independently, including partial success and failure cases.
Token-use idempotency reloads existing rows on conflict and rejects durable mismatches instead of treating `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` as success.
Persistence failures keep affected requests in `persistingCompletion` with subreason and last error until retry, replay/import ack, requeue, or recovery closeout succeeds.

userStories.title: Implement rollout cleanup preservation
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want startup rollout cleanup to preserve and replay completion evidence before deleting active runtime rows so fresh-start rollout does not lose durable results.
acceptanceCriteria: Startup phases run before scheduler, claim loop, dispatch loop, or request runtime can scan or admit work: preserve/import completion or token-use evidence, record owner-backed closeout intents, close owner claims, delete/recreate discarded runtime rows, then assign local job state.
Local jobs remain `draining` while unexported, unimported, legacy-pending, or quarantined local completion evidence remains; plain `failed` is used only after no preserved evidence remains.
Owner-backed closeout intent is durable in `completion_outbox` or `pending_token_use` before any owner call and survives local `accepted_claim` deletion.
Cleanup is idempotent across crashes between local outbox import, owner replay, owner closeout ack, local runtime row deletion, and local parent-job state assignment.

userStories.title: Add legacy evidence repair path
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want pre-plan durable completion evidence without exact attempt ids to remain importable through a named repair path instead of being silently discarded.
acceptanceCriteria: Legacy outbox, ack, pending-token-use, and token-use rows without exact `requestAttemptId`s are converted, kept pending repair, or quarantined through named restart-safe states before new exact-attempt invariants apply.
Safe legacy import creates deterministic `legacyRequestAttemptId`s from durable row identity and records a `legacyRolloutImported` closeout marker.
Legacy rows that cannot be safely imported keep the local job `draining` with `legacyCompletionEvidencePendingRepair` or `legacyCompletionEvidenceQuarantined` and remain in repair/import query scope.
The legacy path preserves original durable row references for idempotent rerun and late-conflict tracing, but does not add legacy scheduling/resume fallback for active runtime rows.

userStories.title: Add provider admission lease table
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a focused live-only DuckDB provider admission lease table so request and probe admission share one authoritative provider-wide physical-call cap.
acceptanceCriteria: Add DuckDB table `app.provider_admission_lease` through the existing DuckDB migration flow as a live-only table with provider key, lease kind, lease identity, request/probe ids, holder token, acquired/heartbeat/expiry timestamps, shape checks, uniqueness, and expiry index.

Lease identity is `request:${requestAttemptId}` for request leases and `probe:${endpointAvailabilityKey}:${probeAttemptId}` for probe leases so nullable unique behavior cannot weaken identity enforcement.
Closed lease history and quarantine evidence are not retained in `app.provider_admission_lease`; closeout and recovery evidence stay on manifest, outbox, ack, token-use, or diagnostic surfaces.
Provider lease timing constants use injectable owner clock and are covered by tests.

userStories.title: Implement fenced lease acquire semantics
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want provider lease acquire to be serialized, fenced, version-aware, and idempotent so concurrent workers cannot over-admit or mutate another holder's lease.
acceptanceCriteria: Only the current DuckDB owner admission service writes `app.provider_admission_lease`; non-owner processes and judge workers proxy to the current owner.
Acquire validates owner fencing first and serializes all acquire, heartbeat, release, and expiry operations per `providerKey` until the DuckDB transaction commits or rolls back.
Same-holder idempotent reacquire returns the existing lease before stale-version rejection without changing occupancy, holder identity, `acquired_at_ms`, heartbeat, or expiry timestamps.

Every non-idempotent acquire validates current `providerLimitVersion`, reconciles only allowed stale rows, counts remaining request plus probe leases including suspect fresh-holder rows, and inserts only below current owner-side `providerLimit`.
Acquire returns `alreadyHeld`, `staleProviderLimitSnapshot`, or capacity failure without admitting when required by holder identity, version, or cap state.

userStories.title: Implement lease heartbeat and reconciliation
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want lease heartbeat, release, demotion, and cleanup to preserve healthy holders while freeing capacity after durable terminal closeout or proven stale holders.
acceptanceCriteria: Heartbeat and holder release are compare-and-update/delete operations scoped by full holder token and are idempotent `notHolder` no-ops for non-matching holders.
Heartbeat may extend only the exact held lease across provider-limit-version changes and cannot create, replace, move, or change lease ownership/provider keys.
`admissionOwnerDemotion` fails closed and cannot mutate lease rows; `holderWorkerDemotion` is holder freshness state used only by the current fenced owner for reconciliation.

Startup and worker-loss cleanup release exact request leases with durable terminal request-attempt closeout, expire stale/missing/demoted holder leases after grace rules, and count suspect fresh-holder leases until exact proof allows deletion.
Probe leases are never closed by request-attempt terminal closeout and require holder release, stale/missing/demoted reconciliation, or suspect-fresh proof for the exact probe identity.

userStories.title: Integrate request leases into withJudgmentRequest
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want normal LLM requests to acquire provider request leases through `withJudgmentRequest` before sending so local counters cannot admit above the provider-wide cap.
acceptanceCriteria: `withJudgmentRequest` is the only normal LLM request admission point and requests provider request lease acquire/release around the physical LLM call.
Local `localProviderLiveRequests` increments only after successful request lease acquire and drops in scoped cleanup/finalizer when the physical call ends, before persistence continues.
If owner fencing rejects release after ownership changes, local cleanup still completes and shared-row deletion is left to current-owner reconciliation.
Request attempt ids are generated and written to durable manifest surfaces before an attempt enters `waitingForRequestSlot`.
Provider limit decreases allow existing calls to finish but admit no new request or probe leases until held physical calls fall below the new limit.

userStories.title: Add endpoint probe permits and leases
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want endpoint recovery probes to use separate bounded probe permits and shared probe leases so probes can recover endpoints without consuming normal request slots or exceeding the physical provider cap.
acceptanceCriteria: Endpoint probes use separate scoped in-memory probe permits plus shared provider probe leases and never increment request-level `Live LLM calls`.

Each worker holds at most one live probe per endpoint availability key, uses cooldown/backoff, and releases local permit plus shared probe lease on success, failure, interruption, shutdown, or demotion.
Successful probes only mark endpoint health and wake normal waiters; judged LLM work must reacquire normal request admission before invoking the model.
Probe waiters subscribe to provider lease release and probe cooldown changes and are cancellable on worker shutdown, demotion, provider/job closeout, and endpoint recovery.
Probe diagnostics expose local and observed aggregate probe live counts separately from request fill metrics.

userStories.title: Add lifecycle telemetry reconciliation
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want prompt and request lifecycle telemetry to reconcile after worker loss without reporting stale in-memory stages as precise live state.
acceptanceCriteria: Dispatch telemetry records prompt lifecycle states and request telemetry records separate request-attempt lifecycle states with per-state counts and age/duration summaries by job id, provider key, lifecycle kind, and request attempt id where applicable.

Lifecycle ownership is explicit across claim, dispatch queue, preparation, slot wait, live request, request closeout persistence, prompt terminal cleanup, worker-loss recovery, and terminal prompt cleanup.

Derived prompt-state precedence handles multiple attempts, active attempts, persisting attempts, unavailable diagnostics, terminal success, and terminal closure without treating retry/superseded `closedRequest` attempts as prompt terminal failure.
Worker crash or telemetry loss preserves SQLite/journal-derived queue truth and marks unavailable in-memory stages as `telemetryUnavailable` or `workerUnavailable` rather than stale bottleneck ages.
Durable manifest attempts reconcile independently from lease cleanup and recover waiting or live attempts without creating duplicate attempt ids.

userStories.title: Implement prompt terminal cleanup rules
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want prompt terminal cleanup to distinguish request-attempt terminal states from prompt terminal states so zero-request and recovery cases close explicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: Prompt terminal `completed` is written only after prompt terminal cleanup succeeds, no active/pending/retry/requeue work remains, and at least one success-producing attempt completed or an explicit no-request success reason exists.

Prompts with zero request attempts can complete only through named successful no-request reasons such as `alreadyJudged`; enqueue rejection, skipped dispatch, halt, cancellation, recovery, missing data, fulltext failures, rollout cleanup, and similar non-success paths close with explicit reasons.

Unavailable diagnostics are periodically repaired by exact durable evidence, requeue with old attempt closure, or conversion to `closedRequest` with an explicit recovery closeout reason after the repair deadline.

Cleanup covers enqueue rejection, connection halt, worker shutdown, `admissionOwnerDemotion`, prompt recovery, article/prompt missing data, fulltext failures, request failure, and persistence failure.

userStories.title: Expose canonical provider telemetry fields
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want job detail and worker telemetry to expose lease-authoritative provider fields, observed aggregate fields, and source metadata so scheduling decisions and UI diagnostics are not ambiguous.
acceptanceCriteria: Telemetry exposes canonical fields including provider limit/version, leased request/probe/physical calls, available request leases, normal request capacity, target live calls, request fill percentages, local live counts, local target/share/headroom fields, allocation fields, observed aggregate fields, backlog fields, endpoint diagnostics, bottleneck, and `convergenceDiagnostics`.

Observed aggregate telemetry is labeled best-effort and never used as admission authority; missing or slow remote telemetry is `telemetryUnavailable` diagnostics, not a reason to reduce request admission beyond shared lease results.
Telemetry source metadata includes local worker id, fresh/stale/unavailable worker counts, aggregate completeness, and per-provider/per-endpoint coverage metadata.
Route contracts expose every `convergenceDiagnostics` member, including `preconditionsStableSinceMs` and `preconditionChangedReason`, rather than an opaque summary string.
Old `providerActive*` fields are removed or split into request-lease, local prompt/pipeline, and observed telemetry fields in the same API/UI contract change.

userStories.title: Compute provider target allocation snapshots
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the current owner to publish complete target allocation snapshots so workers do not compute divergent local shares from partial telemetry.
acceptanceCriteria: Owner computes `providerTargetAllocationSnapshot` with `providerAllocationVersion` for each `providerKey`/`providerLimitVersion`/`providerProbeOccupancyVersion` from the owner worker registry, current probe occupancy, and fresh routeability reports.

Snapshot includes `providerProbeOccupancyVersion`, `probeOccupancySampledAtMs`, `allocationInputState`, `allocationCompleteCurrent`, per-worker `expectedLocalLiveShare`, `unallocatedTargetLiveCalls`, and source metadata for incomplete inputs.
`normalRequestCapacity`, `targetRequestLiveCalls`, and each routeable worker's `effectiveProviderLimit` are computed from the same snapshot input.

Allocation distributes integer target shares deterministically over stable provider/worker order, respects each worker effective capacity, redistributes unused share, and stops when target calls are allocated or fresh routeable capacity is exhausted.

Probe acquire, release, and reconciliation increments `providerProbeOccupancyVersion`, invalidates older snapshots, and prevents stale allocation snapshots from increasing target/share or new claiming.

userStories.title: Implement adaptive backlog controller
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want adaptive prompt and request-work backlog targets so ready work keeps provider request leases fed without treating prompt concurrency as the provider cap.
acceptanceCriteria: Define controller constants with explicit units for prompt and request-work backlog min/max, drain windows, successful lease windows, stage-age thresholds, low-limit integer rounding, hysteresis bands, and immediate safety-clamp rules.

Controller computes prompt and request-work backlog targets from provider limits, probe occupancy, shared lease availability, effective capacity, local live requests, local backlog, active/queued prompts, ready count, chunk estimates, drain rate, endpoint availability, and lifecycle ages.

Controller separates target adjustment from replenishment: replenish to existing targets whenever ready work and higher-priority rules allow, but increase targets only under target-fill/drain evidence with available provider and local capacity.
Local target gap and additional lease headroom are derived separately and capped by provider-wide available request leases and owner allocation share.

Immediate reductions apply for provider limit/probe changes, worker freshness, endpoint routeability, effective capacity, or incomplete allocation snapshots; upward target/share increases use hysteresis.
Owner-backed ready-work signal or claim-result fallback distinguishes `noReadyWork` from underfed request admission.

userStories.title: Add dynamic preparation and request-work accounting
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want dynamic preparation concurrency, interruptible waiters, and chunked request-work accounting so request pressure is visible without using prompt concurrency as the request cap.
acceptanceCriteria: Prompt preparation concurrency is dynamic instead of fixed at `16` and bounded by safe minimum/maximum limits.
Prompts waiting for request slots are tracked separately from prompts doing preparation.
Worker, fallback, and Codex request-slot waiters are scoped and removed or rejected on prompt recovery, worker shutdown, demotion, connection halt, and request failure.

Chunked judging consumes one provider request slot per active LLM request, contributes multiple units to request-work backlog, counts as at least one request-work unit before exact chunk estimates are known, and reports each request attempt separately in telemetry.
Prompt/pipeline concurrency remains high enough to avoid underfeeding request admission but is never used as the request cap.

userStories.title: Implement bottleneck classification
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want stable bottleneck classification and convergence diagnostics so job-detail responses explain why provider live requests are below target.
acceptanceCriteria: Classification precedence is completion persistence, endpoint unavailable, effective capacity limited, worker capacity, fallback capacity, provider saturated, provider at target, prompt preparation, request slot wait, claiming, then no ready work.

Subreason groups do not overlap primary bottleneck enums, and request-slot waits require concrete subreasons such as owner admission unavailable, stale snapshot refresh pending, waiter not woken, acquire contention, no acquire attempt recorded, or interrupted.

Provider at target is distinct from provider saturated: at-target means request leases reached target while physical calls remain below provider limit; saturated means physical calls reached provider limit or acquire failed at the provider cap.
`convergenceDiagnostics` reports explicit preconditions, stable window timing, allocation completeness, active higher-priority stop rules, and precondition-change reason.

Under stable convergence preconditions, responses either reach `targetRequestLiveCalls` or report a canonical bottleneck with required subreason/source metadata; zero-live cases use the same convergence exceptions.

userStories.title: Update judgment job API contracts
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want judgment job APIs and admin runtime routes to expose the new lifecycle, provider, allocation, and bottleneck read models consistently across web and desktop consumers.
acceptanceCriteria: Update `/api/judgmentsjobs/:id`, judgment job health responses, `/api/admin/judgment-dispatch-runtime/:jobId`, Eden/API types, and route read models with canonical telemetry/API field names.

API responses distinguish lease-authoritative fields from observed best-effort fields and include endpoint diagnostics keyed by `endpointAvailabilityKey` with local probe state, observed probe live counts, cooldown, endpoint identity, and provider-level summary.
`Claimed`, `Running Prompts`, `Worker active prompts`, `Worker queued prompts`, and `Live LLM calls` use consistent lifecycle definitions based on provider key and claim/request lifecycle state.
Route/API tests cover crash containment, route read model consistency, provider diagnostics, bottleneck subreasons, and telemetry source metadata.
Shared API changes compile for both browser/web and desktop flows.

userStories.title: Update admin jobs telemetry UI
userStories.description: As an admin user, I want the job detail UI to show request-level provider capacity, prompt/request-work backlogs, allocation state, and endpoint diagnostics clearly so I can understand why judging is claiming, waiting, or held.
acceptanceCriteria: `/admin/jobs/:id` displays lease-authoritative provider metrics separately from observed aggregate telemetry and local worker diagnostics.
UI renames or splits existing `providerActive*`/active prompt fields so request-level metrics cannot be confused with prompt or pipeline slots.

UI shows local prompt backlog and request-work backlog versus targets, expected local live share, local target and lease headroom, allocation state, convergence diagnostics, bottleneck and subreason/source metadata, and endpoint probe state when claiming is held.
UI labels observed aggregate telemetry as best-effort/partial when remote telemetry is missing or partial.
Browser web flow verifies the admin jobs page loads and explains underfed provider, endpoint unavailable, provider at target, provider saturated, and completion persistence states.
Desktop build verifies the shared admin UI and route contracts still compile for desktop.

userStories.title: Verify robust send plan quality gates
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the full robust send implementation verified with the PRD's final gates so the server, database, client, browser, and desktop flows are complete.
acceptanceCriteria: All user stories are implemented without changing model, provider, thinking level, runtime model, saved `maxInflightRequests`, or provider connection settings as part of scheduling behavior.
Convergence success criteria pass for ready work with stable provider acceptance, positive normal request capacity, complete current allocation, and no higher-priority stop rules.
Provider physical calls never exceed `providerLimit` outside explicit limit-decrease drain-down, and no new request or probe lease is admitted during over-limit drain-down.

After startup and worker-loss reconciliation, each worker reports local live request counts matching held request leases and provider-wide admission uses shared lease acquire results rather than observed telemetry.
